correctness.rationale: For an orbit with primitive period p, exactly n/p reflected rotations fix each of its p representatives, giving n fixed pairs and hence a 1/n reflection-count formula, including nonprimitive necklaces. Odd lengths and vertex-axis reflections require a letter equal to its fixed-point-free complement, hence impossible. At even n, n/2 edge-axis reflections each fix one word per linear length-n/2 halfstring with capped runs and half the GC count; their junctions always have complementary (unequal) bases. Therefore F_m(n,g)=L_m(n/2,g/2)/2 when n,g even, otherwise zero. Primitive-power decomposition gives Möbius inversion. Run-type transfer with A/T and C/G, two initial letter choices and 1 or 2 run transitions derives H=2(a+b+2ab)/(1−a−b−3ab). For fixed m, primitive finite-state strong aperiodicity plus pole analysis gives the stated λ_m^{n/2}/√n asymptotic and positive variance. Independently brute-enumerated all cyclic rotation necklaces and reverse complements for 132 GC-composition/cap/length cells n≤8. The all-length claim follows from the reflection proof, not this enumeration.

value.rationale: Joint reverse-complement symmetry, GC composition and cyclic homopolymer caps are naturally motivated in DNA sequence design. The result counts all fixed rotation orbits, including primitive ones, not merely constructs codebooks; it yields exact finite counts and a sharp asymptotic for an infinite constrained family. This is a useful complete enumerative invariant rather than a generic unweighted transfer-matrix rewrite.
